title: Monday, September 14, 2026

headline.title: The AI trade just split in two, and it split on an essay rather than a number. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a piece Saturday calling on the industry to slow the pace at which it advances model capabilities — Sam Altman (“I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier”) and Elon Musk (“Dario is right”) both endorsed it within hours. The FT reported investors reading it straight through to lower AI infrastructure capex, and Barclays' Emmanuel Cau said a greater focus on safety raises questions about the pace of that spending. Nothing about demand changed. No guidance moved. The semis are being repriced on a thesis about the future, not a datapoint about the present.
headline.summary: But look at who is actually down. The sellers of AI are being destroyed — VRT −8.85%, ARM −7.66%, INTC −6.86%, SNDK −6.08%, MU −5.96%, AMD −5.70%, QCOM −5.69%. The buyers of AI are green: META +2.00%, GOOGL +1.45%, MSFT +0.55%. Early wire copy had the hyperscalers falling with the group; by 7:35 CT they had separated cleanly. That divergence is the whole trade. If the industry genuinely slows capex, the hyperscalers are the ones who stop writing the checks and the chipmakers are the ones who stop cashing them.

overview:
Two unrelated stories are hitting the same session, and they push in opposite directions. The first is the AI-safety repricing above. The second is oil, where the single headline this book has named for a week as the trade-ender arrived and did the opposite of what was expected. The Hormuz meeting in Muscat — the one Sunday's Week Ahead built its Monday around — was postponed. Oman said it was being put off “in the interests of consensus” after Yemen's Houthis attacked a military airbase in Saudi Arabia. Worse for supply: Saudi Arabia shut its East-West crude pipeline in the Riyadh and Madinah regions after drone attacks, which per Rystad leaves the Strait of Hormuz as the kingdom's only route for moving large volumes of crude westward. The bypass is gone. WTI +2.6% to $102.66, Brent +2.7% to $107.38 — a four-month high, on top of a 9% week. USO +2.83% premarket and the whole complex bid: OXY +2.02%, COP +1.56%, CVX +1.53%, XOM +1.51%.

And the Fed decides into exactly this on Wednesday. Futures now price an 87% chance of a 25bp hike (up from 85% Friday, and 44% a month ago). Note what oil does to that call: Oxford Economics said Friday it expects a third consecutive set of moderate inflation readings to tip a narrow majority toward holding, but that rising oil prices and still-elevated inflation make a risk-management case for a hike. Every additional dollar of crude this morning strengthens the hawkish argument for a rate move that cannot do anything about the price of crude. Yields are not confirming, though — the 2-year fell 1.8bp to 4.63% and the 10-year eased to 4.96%, and gold is down 1.9% to $4,327, which is not the behavior of a market pricing panic.

Two things the tape is saying that the headline is not. First, Friday was an AI-infrastructure melt-up — DELL and HPE both closed +12% at records and semis rose 2% as a group. This morning's red is a violent reversal of Friday's best trade, not a continuation of a decline. Second, the escalation is worse than a postponement: the US and Iran traded strikes on vessels in the Strait, and reports flag up to 4% of global supply at risk. Also on deck this week that the Sunday map missed: the BoJ decides alongside the BoE, and Wednesday's FOMC carries a new dot plot.

setups: Buyers green, sellers red — on the same headline

This is the cleanest expression of the morning and it is not a single ticker, it is a pair. The AI-safety essay is a bearish datapoint for anyone whose revenue is AI capex and an ambiguous-to-bullish one for anyone whose margin is reduced by AI capex. META +2.00%, GOOGL +1.45%, MSFT +0.55% against VRT −8.85%, ARM −7.66%, MU −5.96%, AMD −5.70%. Early wire copy grouped them together and the tape separated them within the hour. The risk: this is a one-morning divergence off an opinion piece, not a demand print, and it can snap back just as fast on a single Trump comment — he already pushed back Sunday, calling the concerns “very negative forces… bringing up things that won't happen.”

Every energy setup this book carried last week named the Hormuz meeting as the single headline that ends the trade. It arrived, and it was postponed — Oman shelved it after the Houthi strike on a Saudi airbase. The escalation matters more than the cancellation: Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline, which Rystad says leaves Hormuz as the kingdom's only large-volume westward route. Brent $107.38, a four-month high, after a 9% week. The lesson is the one the Week Ahead led with in different words — a meeting was never a reopening, and now there is not even a meeting. The risk: this is now a crowded, extended long into a Fed that may hike partly because of it.
Dreamforce bid, into a fade pattern

Up on the eve of the keynote, which is exactly the setup our own five-event study says to distrust: Dreamforce is not a volatility event — 1.06x volume and 1.21 ATR in 2025, 0.91x and 0.76 ATR in 2024, and it faded both years (−3.36%, −1.36%). Three of the five investor days in that study gapped up and closed below the open. CRM is gapping up. Keynote is Tuesday 12:00p CT; the Investor & Analyst Session that actually carries a financial framework is Wednesday 3:00p CT.

darkpool.note: The names that soaked up Friday's after-hours size are exactly where this morning's red is concentrated. LRCX took $600M (mixed, AH) and is −8.4%; SNDK $449M (ask, AH) is −6.1%; NVDA $407M (bid, AH) read bid into a −2.6% morning. Mixed size is interest, not direction, so LRCX's is a lean and not a verdict — but the clustering is the point. The exception is the one that matters for today's thesis: META drew the largest ex-ETF print on the board at $700M at the ask, a second straight night above $600M, and it is the name trading +2.00% while its own supply chain is down 6–9%. On cumulative flow META sits third at $2.8B (ask) behind MU $4.0B (mixed) and NVDA $3.5B (bid). Morning prints found the same names again: NVDA $50M (ask), LRCX $44M (ask), GOOGL $44M (bid) — and EWY $62M (mixed), the South Korea ETF, hours after the Kospi fell 3.6%. Chips are coloured by side on the standard reading — ask is the buyer paying up, bid is the seller hitting, mixed is interest without direction. This morning's tape agrees with that reading: META's ask print is +2.00% and NVDA's bid print is −2.60%.
